text: The men of Israel had sworn an oath at Mizpah: "None of us will give his daughter in marriage to a Benjaminite."
So the people came to Bethel and sat there before God until evening, and they lifted up their voices and wept bitterly.
They said, "Why, LORD, God of Israel, has this happened in Israel, that today one tribe should be missing from Israel?"
Early the next morning the people built an altar there and offered burnt offerings and fellowship offerings.

Then the Israelites asked, "Which of all the tribes of Israel failed to come up to the LORD with the assembly?" For they had bound themselves with a solemn oath that anyone who did not come up to the LORD at Mizpah should be put to death.
The Israelites grieved for their brother Benjamin and said, "Today one tribe has been cut off from Israel.
What shall we do about wives for those who are left, since we have sworn by the LORD not to give them any of our daughters in marriage?"
Then they asked, "Which one of the tribes of Israel did not come up to the LORD at Mizpah?" And it turned out that no one from Jabesh Gilead had come to the camp, to the assembly.
For when the people were counted, not one of the inhabitants of Jabesh Gilead was there.
So the assembly sent twelve thousand fighting men there with these orders: "Go and put the inhabitants of Jabesh Gilead to the sword, including the women and children.
This is what you are to do: devote to destruction every male, and every woman who has slept with a man."
Among the inhabitants of Jabesh Gilead they found four hundred young virgins who had never slept with a man, and they brought them to the camp at Shiloh in the land of Canaan.
Then the whole assembly sent word to the Benjaminites at the rock of Rimmon, offering them peace.
So the Benjaminites returned at that time, and they were given the women of Jabesh Gilead who had been spared. But there were not enough for them all.
The people grieved for Benjamin, because the LORD had made a gap in the tribes of Israel.
And the elders of the assembly said, "What shall we do about wives for those who are left, since the women of Benjamin have been wiped out?"
They said, "The survivors of Benjamin must have heirs, so that a tribe of Israel will not be blotted out.
Yet we cannot give them our own daughters as wives, for the Israelites have sworn: 'Cursed be anyone who gives a wife to Benjamin.'"
Then they said, "Look, there is the yearly festival of the LORD at Shiloh, which lies north of Bethel, east of the road that goes up from Bethel to Shechem, and south of Lebonah."
So they instructed the Benjaminites: "Go and hide in the vineyards
and watch. When the young women of Shiloh come out to join in the dancing, rush from the vineyards, and each of you seize a wife from the young women of Shiloh, and go to the land of Benjamin.

When their fathers or brothers come to us with a complaint, we will say to them, 'Be kind to us and let them keep these young women, since we did not capture a wife for each man in the war. And you are not guilty, for you yourselves did not give your daughters to them.'"

versions.text: When their fathers or brothers come to us with a complaint, we will say to them, 'Do us the favor of letting them keep the women, since we did not get wives for them in the war. And you are not guilty, since you did not give your daughters to them.'"
versions.explanation: "Do us the favor of letting them keep the women" is wordy and the two uses of "them" are ambiguous when heard aloud; the clarified wording also reflects the Hebrew "we did not take each man his wife in the war" more closely.

text: So that is what the Benjaminites did. They carried off as many wives as they needed from the dancers, and they went back to their own inheritance, rebuilt the towns, and settled in them.
At that time the Israelites left that place, each going to his own tribe and clan; each one set out for his own inheritance.

versions.text: At that time the Israelites also left, each going to his own tribe and clan, each returning from there to his own inheritance.
versions.explanation: "left" followed by "returning from there" is redundant and stumbles when read aloud; also "also" has no basis in the Hebrew. The suggested wording keeps both Hebrew clauses (departing from there / going out to his inheritance) with a cleaner rhythm.

text: In those days there was no king in Israel; everyone did as he saw fit.
